curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `q{register}…q`; `@{register}`; `@@`; counts such as `10@a`; append with `qA`; inspect, put, and edit macro text; stable anchors; deliberate final cursor position; stopping on failed motion/search; optional recursion
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Record a robust transformation, replay it safely, inspect or repair it, and state the assumptions that make it valid
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Comment irregular calls; restructure repeated object entries; record on one row and apply to selected instances; repair a macro with a bad final motion
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core automation. Recursive macros are optional and never required for normal progression

lessons.title: Record once, replay deliberately
lessons.objective: Record a complete transformation in a named register and replay it safely.

activities.title: A macro is recorded Normal-mode intent
activities.body: q followed by a register starts recording. Press q again in Normal mode to stop; @ followed by the register replays those keys from the current cursor.
activities.contrast: A macro stores keys and their assumptions, not an abstract refactor.

activities.title: Silence three API calls
activities.instruction: Record adding "// " at the line start, then replay it on the next two rows.

commandGroups.explanation: Record one complete line-start insertion in register a.
Move to the next row and replay register a.
Move once more and replay the latest macro.

hints: Name the register and decide exactly where replay should begin.
Record one complete, repeatable transformation before replaying it.
Watch the final cursor position: it becomes the next replay's starting point.

feedback.success: The macro completed the intended transformation.
feedback.why: The recorded keys reused a named register while preserving a predictable starting point.
feedback.contrast: A brittle macro would depend on a column or continue after its assumptions stopped matching.

activities.portability: Uses named-register macro behavior shared by Vim and conforming Vim integrations.

activities.title: Choose the smallest safe automation
activities.prompt: Several nonadjacent rows need the same multi-step structural edit, and each has the same reliable anchor. Which tool should you try first?
activities.explanation: The transformation is multi-step and structural, while search can deliberately select its nonadjacent instances.

activities.title: Macros are tiny programs with contracts
activities.body: Record from a stable start, finish at a deliberate cursor position, replay only where the assumptions hold, and inspect the register when the program needs repair. Recursive macros exist, but they remain optional because safe ordinary replay is the core skill.
takeaways: qa…q records; @a replays; @@ repeats the latest macro.
qA appends, and register text can be put, edited, and yanked back.
A failed anchor should stop replay before later keys can cause damage.

notes: Replay starts at the current cursor.

reference.purpose: Repeat a self-advancing macro a trusted number of times.
notes: A failed anchor stops remaining iterations.

reference.purpose: Build macro steps around durable textual structure.
notes: Avoid absolute columns across irregular rows.

reference.purpose: Choose where the next replay begins.
notes: Record movement only when every replay should advance.

reference.purpose: Append keys to register a without replacing it.
notes: Inspect before extending an unfamiliar macro.

reference.purpose: Put macro text, edit it, and write it back.
